E1.text:
Thus replacing $H_1$ by $H_1'$ gives a nontoroidal graph.
By Corollary~\ref{common:reduced-forms}, $H_1$ is among the
candidates with attachment set $A$ and added edges $E$.
Of the $26{,}633$ candidates, $14$ are excluded because they have no
vertex-disjoint $s_1$--$t_1$ and $s_2$--$t_2$ paths. For every other
candidate, adjoining $H_2$ gives a graph with a $K_5$ minor, a cut
of at most two vertices, or a proper nontoroidal minor~\supp{E1}.
Hence no bridge contains such a path.

E2.text:
Taking $B'=B$ shows that $B+ac+cd+bd$ is nonplanar. It is a minor
of $G$, obtained by retaining $B$ and $cd$ and shortening $apc$
and $brd$ to $ac$ and $bd$, so it has no $K_5$ minor. By the
equivalence, Corollary~\ref{common:reduced-forms} puts $B$ among
the candidates with attachments $a,b,c,d$ and added edges
$ac,cd,bd$. For each of the $15{,}626$ candidates, the graph
$(\Psi_1\cup B)+af$ has an edge whose deletion or contraction is
nontoroidal~\supp{E2}, a contradiction. Thus $B$ has a disk drawing
in the order $a,b,d,c$, and Lemma~\ref{dis:four-root-isolation}
gives that $D$ is a single vertex.

E3.text:
Suppose every bridge with at least two interior vertices has
three attachments and a planar relevant completion. By
Lemma~\ref{dis:relevant}, these bridges have the forms in
Proposition~\ref{prop:three-root-disjoint}. We combine them with
bridges with one interior vertex and the permitted edges, keeping
the interiors disjoint and using the attachment restrictions and
Lemma~\ref{dis:counts}. Four bridges with the same four attachments
would give a $K_{4,4}$ and hence a $K_5$ minor, so we allow at most
three. We use~\supp{E3} when all three paths are edges
and~\supp{E4} when some path has an internal vertex.

We keep the graphs satisfying Lemmas~\ref{lem:independent-neighborhood}(a)
and~\ref{dis:four-root-isolation}. By Lemma~\ref{dis:opposite-order},
we exclude graphs with disjoint $s_i$--$t_j$ and $s_j$--$t_i$ paths
through distinct bridges. By~\supp{E3}, each remaining graph is a
subgraph of a recorded toroidal graph or contains a recorded
nontoroidal graph. Since $G$ is a minor obstruction, it equals one
of the latter. All but $\mathfrak T_{48}$ and $\mathfrak T_{58}$ have a
proper nontoroidal minor, and neither has a four-attachment bridge
in this case. Together with $\mathfrak T_5$,
$\mathfrak T_{68}$ and $\mathfrak T_{69}$, these give the stated list.

E4.text:
Suppose every bridge with at least two interior vertices has
three attachments and a planar relevant completion. By
Lemma~\ref{dis:relevant}, these bridges have the forms in
Proposition~\ref{prop:three-root-disjoint}. We combine them with
bridges with one interior vertex and the permitted edges, keeping
the interiors disjoint and using the attachment restrictions and
Lemma~\ref{dis:counts}. Four bridges with the same four attachments
would give a $K_{4,4}$ and hence a $K_5$ minor, so we allow at most
three. We use~\supp{E3} when all three paths are edges
and~\supp{E4} when some path has an internal vertex.

These choices include $G$ without having to specify the paths inside
each candidate. By the coverage check in~\supp{E4}, each graph in
this family is a subgraph of a recorded toroidal graph or contains
a recorded nontoroidal graph. Since $G$ is nontoroidal, minimality
gives equality with one of the latter. With at least
one $s_mt_m$ absent, the checks leave $\mathfrak T_{32},\mathfrak
T_{43},\mathfrak T_{61}$ when every bridge has at most one interior
vertex, and $\mathfrak T_{38},\mathfrak T_{45},\mathfrak T_{48},
\mathfrak T_{66},\mathfrak T_{67}$ when some bridge has form $T,S$
or $Q$. No graph with a four-cycle form remains.

E5.text:
For each of the six choices of $H_0$, we require the subdivision in
Construction~\ref{common:marked-construction} to contain the edges
identified above for that choice. Adding $J_1\cup J_2$, the edges
$cf,ed$, and the chosen additions to each candidate for $B$ gives
$1{,}586$ candidates for $G$. Each has a $K_5$ minor, a cut of at
most two vertices, or a proper nontoroidal minor, except for
$\mathfrak T_{21}$ and $\mathfrak T_{63}$~\supp{E5}.

E6.text:
The paths $P_x,P_y,s_xps_y,t_xrt_y$ give $B\cup C$ as a minor
of $G$, so it has no $K_5$ minor. Every $K_{3,3}$ subdivision
in $B\cup C$ uses $s_yt_y$, since deleting that edge leaves the
planar completion above. Corollary~\ref{common:reduced-forms}
with $H_0=C$ and $s_yt_y$ required in the subdivision gives
$1{,}378$ candidate bridges. Here $B\cup K_4[A]$ is
three-connected, Lemma~\ref{dis:opposite-order} excludes disjoint
$s_x$--$t_y$ and $s_y$--$t_x$ paths through $B$, and every
degree-three vertex has independent neighbors by
Lemma~\ref{lem:independent-neighborhood}(a). The checks
in~\supp{E6} leave two labeled bridges. Up to interchanging $A_1,A_2$,
the interior is $\{p',q',v\}$, with
\[
N(p')=N(q')=\{s_x,s_y,v\},
\]
and its remaining edges are $vt_x,vt_y$.

E7.text:
The paths $apc,brd$ and the edge $cd$ give $B\cup H_0$ as a minor
of $G$, so it has no $K_5$ minor. Every $K_{3,3}$ subdivision in it
uses $cd$, since $B+ac+bd$ is planar. Corollary~\ref{common:reduced-forms}
with $cd$ required gives $2{,}104$ candidates. Here $B\cup K_4[A]$
is three-connected, $L$ has no $K_5$ minor, and no degree-three
interior vertex is adjacent to both ends of $cd$ by
Lemma~\ref{lem:independent-neighborhood}(a). With the planarity
conditions above, the checks in~\supp{E7} leave nine labeled
bridges, giving the five displayed forms up to interchanging $A_1,A_2$.

In case (i) of Lemma~\ref{dis:type-b-forms}, the nine labeled bridges
and the two choices of added edge give $18$ graphs. Sixteen have a
proper nontoroidal minor and the other two are isomorphic to
$\mathfrak T_{66}$~\supp{E7}. Suppose (ii) holds. Replacing $ce,df$
in the nonplanar simple-face test by $cqe,dzf$ gives a connected
nonplanar subgraph $S$ of $G-aq$. In a torus embedding of this proper
minor, every face of $S$ is a disk by Lemma~\ref{lem:torus-complement}.

E8.text:
For $E=\varnothing$, the construction gives $57{,}479$ bridges up to
isomorphisms fixing the attachments. The enumeration in~\supp{E8}
checks each with $(n_c,n_d)=(2,2),(3,2),(3,3)$. It leaves the
fourteen graphs in the first list, all with $(n_c,n_d)=(2,2)$.
For $E=\{ab,ac,bc\}$, the same enumeration checks $14{,}638$ bridges
with $(n_c,n_d)=(3,2)$ and leaves only $\mathfrak T_{11}$.
Of the $3\cdot57{,}479+14{,}638=187{,}075$ candidates, every other
graph has a $K_5$ minor, a cut of at most two vertices, or a proper
nontoroidal minor.

E9.text:
Construction~\ref{common:marked-construction} lists the reduced
bridges on $x,c,d$. Splitting $x$ as above gives $2{,}953$ candidates
for $B$ up to isomorphisms fixing the four attachments. We add three
vertices with neighborhood $\{a,b,c\}$ and two with neighborhood
$\{a,b,d\}$ to each. Of the resulting graphs, $2{,}159$ have a $K_5$
minor, $92$ have a cut of at most two vertices, and $702$ have a proper
nontoroidal minor~\supp{E9}. None can be $G$.

E10.text: If $c,d$ lie apart, take one retained form for $D_c$ and one for $D_d$. If exactly one component avoids $c,d$, include one of the eleven bridges of Lemma~\ref{r2:ab-cut-single} and a permitted subset of $\{aw,bw\}$. If two components avoid $c,d$, include the two single vertices adjacent to all of $X$. In this case $aw,bw$ are absent by Lemma~\ref{lem:independent-neighborhood}(a). If $c,d$ lie together, take one retained form for $D_1$ and include those same two single vertices. These choices give $12{,}645$ graphs up to isomorphism, of which $1{,}471$ have $B$ planar. Among these the checks in~\supp{E10} leave only $\mathfrak T_{56},\mathfrak T_{72},\mathfrak T_{73}$. In each, exactly one component of $B-X$ avoids $c,d$.

E11.text:
For each of the three choices of $g_2$, there are two ways to join
$x_1,x_2$ to different vertices of $\{u,v\}$. If both are adjacent
to the same vertex, we have two choices for that vertex and three
choices for the attachment in $\{b,c,d\}$ adjacent to the other.
This gives $3(2+2\cdot3)=24$ path forms. Together with the seven
stars, these are the $31$ forms checked in~\supp{E11}, leaving
exactly $\mathfrak T_{40},\mathfrak T_{53},\mathfrak T_{56},\mathfrak T_{73}$.

E12.text:
Together with $p',q'$ and $\Psi_2$, these choices give the family
in~\supp{E12}. The coverage check shows that each graph in this
family is a subgraph of a recorded toroidal graph or contains a
recorded nontoroidal graph. Since $G$ is nontoroidal, it contains
one of the latter, and minimality gives equality. Among the recorded
graphs in this family, only $\mathfrak T_{51}$ and $\mathfrak T_{72}$
remain. In both, each
$D_g-g$ is empty or connected. Together with the one-component
case, these give the six graphs in the statement.

E13.text:
As in Proposition~\ref{r2:ab-cut-outcome}, we discard a form
if a single allowed deletion or contraction preserves its neighborhood
in $X$, the required connectivity and the planarity conditions in its row.
Combining the remaining forms of $B_1,B_2$ with the permitted
original edges, $p',q'$ with neighborhood $X$, and $\Psi_2$
gives $1{,}229$ candidates up to isomorphism. Each is toroidal, has a
$K_5$ minor, has a cut of at most two vertices, or has a proper
nontoroidal minor~\supp{E13}.

E14.text: The triangle completion of $B_b$ is three-connected by Lemma~\ref{lem:triangle-completion}, since $D_b-b$ is a component of $G-\{b,c,w\}$. It is a minor of $G$, using the internally disjoint paths $bpc$, $bqap'w$ and $cq'w$ for $bc,bw,cw$, so it has no $K_5$ minor. While $D_b$ keeps its neighbors at $c,w$, the four tests depend on $B_b$ only through $B_b+cw+bw$ and $B_b+cw+bc$. Replacing $B_b$ by a proper allowed minor gives an allowed minor of $B$, since its interior stays adjacent to $w$, the vertices $a,c$ keep $p',q'$, and $d$ keeps $w$. By minimality, no such minor keeps both completions nonplanar. Lemma~\ref{core:two-cap-critical}, with $c,w,b$ as $x,y,z$, therefore makes $B_b$ either $Q(b;c,w)$ or one of the two four-cycle forms. The enumeration~\supp{E14} applies Construction~\ref{common:marked-construction} after identifying $c,w$ to a vertex $x$, with attachments $b,x$ and added edge $bx$. It then splits $x$ back into $c,w$, assigning each original edge at $x$ to one of them and adding an edge to an interior vertex at whichever has no interior neighbor. With $\Psi_2$, $p',q'$ and $dw$, the three forms above are among its $24$ candidates. Each has a cut of at most two vertices or a proper nontoroidal minor.

E15.text:
Construction~\ref{common:marked-construction} gives the possible
forms on either side. A segment with ends $b,w$ in $B_b$, or $d,w$
in $B_d$, may be an original edge or a path with one interior
vertex. The two choices of nonplanar completion give $156$
candidates~\supp{E15}. Each has a $K_5$ minor, a cut of at most two
vertices, or a proper nontoroidal minor. This excludes the remaining
case.

E16.text:
Construction~\ref{common:marked-construction} therefore includes
every possible $B_1$, with added edges $bd,cw$, required edge $bd$,
and possible original edges $bw,dw$. Restoring $a$ and the three
pairs of twins gives the $5{,}819$ candidates in~\supp{E16}.
Each has a $K_5$ minor, a cut of at most two vertices, or a proper
nontoroidal minor, a contradiction.

E17.text: Suppose first that every triangle completion is planar. By Lemma~\ref{lem:flat-replacement}, each component outside $\Psi_2$ is a single vertex. There are at most five such vertices, each with neighborhood $\{a,b,c\}$, $\{a,b,d\}$, $\{a,c,d\}$ or $\{b,c,d\}$. There are $\binom{9}{4}=126$ choices for how many have each neighborhood. With $cd$ present or absent, this gives the $252$ choices checked in~\supp{E17}. Only $\mathfrak T_9,\mathfrak T_{10},\mathfrak T_{16}$ remain, all with $cd$ absent.

E18.text: The retained minor is therefore nontoroidal, so by minimality it is $G$. For each of the two possible attachment triples of $B'$, Construction~\ref{common:marked-construction} gives $869$ nonplanar and $120$ planar bridge forms with all three two-edge completions nonplanar. There are three remaining choices for $N(v)$. Each of the resulting $2\cdot3(869+120)=5{,}934$ graphs has a cut of at most two vertices, a $K_5$ minor, or a proper nontoroidal minor~\supp{E18}.

E19.text:
By Lemmas~\ref{r2:component-count} and~\ref{r2:eight-bridge-forms}, we add to $\Psi_2$ one to four of the eight bridge forms, with disjoint interiors and at least one form other than a star. On each attachment triple the eight forms give $19$ labeled bridges up to isomorphisms fixing the attachments. Thus there are $76$ labeled bridges, four of them stars. Choosing at most four with repetition, excluding choices consisting entirely of stars and allowing $cd$ to be present or absent, gives $2\bigl[\binom{80}{4}-\binom{8}{4}\bigr]=3{,}163{,}020$ combinations.

We discard a combination if two twin triples are disjoint, three distinct twin triples share two vertices, or some choice of twin pairs gives a bridge with four attachments. These exclusions also rule out any larger combination containing it. Indeed, only $a,b,c,d$ gain neighbors. The vertices $a,b$ already have degree at least four, and only $a,b$ could be twins of $c$ or $d$, since a twin of $c$ must be adjacent to $p,q$ and a twin of $d$ to $r,z$. Thus the twin pairs keep their neighborhoods, which must be independent in $G$ by Lemma~\ref{lem:independent-neighborhood}(a). A component adjacent to all four attachments remains in a component adjacent to all four.

Any combination containing a smaller nontoroidal one has a proper nontoroidal minor. Of the $3{,}163{,}020$ combinations, \supp{E19} records $2{,}174$ individually. Every other combination contains a smaller one that is nontoroidal or violates one of the conditions above. Of the $2{,}174$ recorded graphs, all but four are toroidal, have a cut of at most two vertices, or have a proper nontoroidal minor. The four remaining graphs are isomorphic to $\mathfrak T_{15}$.

E20.text: The completion $H$ is nonplanar and has no $K_5$ minor. If $bd$ is present, $G-bd$ is toroidal, so $H-bd$ is planar by Corollary~\ref{r1:five-criterion}. Every $K_{3,3}$ subdivision of $H$ then uses $bd$. An allowed reduction of $B$ preserves all five attachments, so the same corollary gives a nontoroidal graph whenever the reduced completion is nonplanar. Corollary~\ref{common:reduced-forms} therefore applies with fixed edges $ab,ac,ad,ae$ and with $bd$ when present. Of the $217{,}376$ candidates, all but eight have a $K_5$ minor, a cut of at most two vertices, or a proper nontoroidal minor~\supp{E20}. The eight are isomorphic to $\mathfrak T_{20},\mathfrak T_{23},\mathfrak T_{38},\mathfrak T_{40}$ or $\mathfrak T_{69}$. In each of the last three graphs, two twin triples are disjoint or meet in two vertices. This leaves $\mathfrak T_{20}$ and $\mathfrak T_{23}$.

E21.text:
Put $H_2=B+bc+de$ and suppose it is nonplanar.
By Lemma~\ref{r1:triangle-minor},
$B+ab+ac+ad+ae+bc+de$ is a minor of $G$.
Thus $H_2$ has no $K_5$ minor. Let $B'$ be an
allowed minor of $B$ with $B'+bc+de$ nonplanar.
The graph $B'+ab+ac+ad+ae+bc+de$ is still a minor
of $G$, so Lemma~\ref{r1:matching-test} makes
$B'+ab+ac+ad+ae$ nonplanar. Thus $\Psi_3\cup B'$
fails both tests of Lemma~\ref{r1:missing-a-criterion}.
Taking $B'=B$, minimality gives $G=\Psi_3\cup B$, and
Corollary~\ref{common:reduced-forms}, with attachments
$b,c,d,e$ and added edges $bc,de$,
includes $B$ among $26{,}633$ forms. Of the resulting graphs,
all but four are toroidal or have a $K_5$ minor or a proper
nontoroidal minor. All four are isomorphic to $\mathfrak T_{54}$~\supp{E21}.

E22.text: Suppose $B_1$ consists of one bridge, with attachments $\{a,b,d\}$ by symmetry. Put $H_4=B_1+ab+ad$. If $H_4$ is nonplanar, deleting $E$ and contracting the interior of $B$ to one vertex still leaves $H_4$ in both tests. By minimality, $E=\varnothing$ and $B$ has one interior vertex. Likewise, no proper allowed reduction of $B_1$ keeps $H_4$ nonplanar. Corollary~\ref{common:reduced-forms}, with added edges $ab,ad$, gives the $349$ forms in~\supp{E22}. Each resulting graph has a $K_5$ minor, a cut of at most two vertices, or a proper nontoroidal minor.

E23.text:
Suppose $B_1+ab+ad$ is planar.
Lemma~\ref{core:three-root-cut} gives twins $p',q'$
whose neighborhood $X$ contains $a$. Since $X$ meets
each of $\{a,b,c\},\{a,d,e\}$ exactly once, it has
the form $\{a,u,v\}$ with
$u,v\in\operatorname{Int}(B_1)$. The same lemma gives
disjoint $b$--$u$ and $d$--$v$ paths.
Choose $p',q',r,z$ as the four twins.
The set $\operatorname{Int}(B)\cup\{b,c,p,q\}$ is
connected because $c$ has a neighbor in the interior of $B$
and $p,q$ join $b$ to $c$. It lies in a component
outside the new $\Psi_3$, with neighbors at $a,d,e$
through $B$ and at $u$ through the $b$--$u$ path.
Since five attachments are excluded, its bridge
has exactly four attachments and at least
$|\operatorname{Int}(B)|+4$ interior vertices, contrary to
the choice of $B$. Thus $B_1+ab+ad$ is nonplanar, and it has no $K_5$ minor.
Let $B_1'$ be an allowed minor of $B_1$ with $B_1'+ab+ad$
nonplanar. Contract the interior of $B$ to $w$
and keep only $\Psi_3$, $B_1'$ and the edges at $w$.
The resulting minor is $\Psi_3\cup B_1'+w$, where
$N(w)=\{a,c,d,e\}$. The graph $\Psi_3+w$ contains $K_{3,3}$ with
parts $\{a,d,e\}$ and $\{r,z,w\}$. Thus, in every torus
embedding of $\Psi_3+w$, each component of the complement
of its closed regular neighborhood is a disk by
Lemma~\ref{lem:torus-complement}.
In every such embedding, a facial walk containing
$a,b,d$ has attachment sequence $abad$, up to
cyclic shift and reversal~\supp{R7}.
Lemma~\ref{cor:boundary-completions} therefore
requires $B_1'+ab+ad$ to be planar, a contradiction.
Hence this minor is nontoroidal. Taking $B_1'=B_1$, minimality
gives $G=\Psi_3\cup B_1+w$, and
Corollary~\ref{common:reduced-forms}, with attachments
$a,b,d$ and added edges $ab,ad$, gives
$349$ possibilities for $B_1$. These are the $349$ forms of
Proposition~\ref{r1:missing-a-outcome} again. Every resulting graph
has a $K_5$ minor, a cut of at most two vertices,
or a proper nontoroidal minor~\supp{E23}.
Thus every other bridge with nonempty interior
has planar triangle completion, and
Lemma~\ref{lem:flat-replacement} makes its interior
a single vertex.
\end{proof}

E24.text: It remains to exclude $n_e=3$. In this case the applicable row gives a single nonplanar completion $B+E'$. It has no $K_5$ minor, since contracting $bd$ into $d$ in the minor of Lemma~\ref{r1:triangle-minor} with $U=B\cup bd$ gives $B+ac+ad+ae+cd+de$. The same row applies after any allowed reduction of $B$, so the resulting graph is nontoroidal whenever its completion is nonplanar. Corollary~\ref{common:reduced-forms} therefore applies with added edges $E'$. This gives $9{,}127$ candidates without $cd$ and $8{,}967$ with $cd$. In each, deleting or contracting one edge gives a nontoroidal minor~\supp{E24}. Thus $n_e=2$, and the first two rows give the claimed form of $G$ and the two nonplanar completions in~\eqref{r1:c1-caps}.

E25.text:
Construction~\ref{common:marked-construction} with added edges $E'$
now includes every possibility, with $de$ required on the subdivision
when $F$ is planar. The two choices of $E$ and the two cases for $F$
give $66{,}384$ candidates. After excluding toroidal graphs and those
with a $K_5$ minor or a proper nontoroidal minor, sixteen candidates
remain, isomorphic to thirteen of the $\mathfrak T_i$~\supp{E25}.
In nine of the thirteen, two twin triples are disjoint or meet in
two vertices, leaving
$\mathfrak T_{14},\mathfrak T_{37},\mathfrak T_{41},\mathfrak T_{59}$.

E26.text:
The same argument applies to any allowed minor $B'$ of $B$ for which
$B'+bc$ is nonplanar. By Corollary~\ref{common:reduced-forms}, it suffices to consider the
$563$ candidates with attachments $b,c,d$ and added edge $bc$.
Of these, $562$ have a proper nontoroidal minor. The remaining graph
is isomorphic to $\mathfrak T_{41}$ and has $B+bd+cd$ planar~\supp{E26},
contrary to the choice of $B$.

E27.text:
In each of these four minors the graph outside $\operatorname{Int}(B)$
is nonplanar, so every face in a torus embedding of that graph is a
disk. On a facial walk meeting $a,b,d$, the sequence restricted to
these vertices is $abad$, with $abd$ also possible when
$N(v)=\{a,c,d\}$~\supp{R10}. Both require $B+ab+ad$ to
be planar by Lemma~\ref{cor:boundary-completions}. Thus the retained
minor is nontoroidal and by minimality is $G$. The same test applies
to every allowed minor of $B$, so Corollary~\ref{common:reduced-forms}
gives $349$ forms with added edges $ab,ad$ for each of the four
choices of $N(v)$. All but two of the resulting graphs have a proper
nontoroidal minor. Both exceptions have $N(v)=\{c,d,e\}$ and
$B+ad+bd$ planar~\supp{E27}, contrary to hypothesis.

E28.text:
If $B+ad$ were nonplanar, Corollary~\ref{common:reduced-forms}
would give $563$ forms with added edge $ad$ for each choice of
$H_1$. All but four of the resulting graphs have a $K_5$ minor or a
proper nontoroidal minor~\supp{E28}. The four exceptions occur when
$cd$ is an edge. In $\mathfrak T_{52}$ and $\mathfrak T_{57}$, two
twin triples meet in two vertices. In $\mathfrak T_{58}$, two are
disjoint. In $\mathfrak T_{59}$, some choice of the four twins gives
a bridge with four attachments.
Thus $B+ad$ is planar.

E29.text:
For $n_c=n_e=2$, the construction gives $31{,}063$ candidates.
Of these, $26{,}502$ have a degree-three vertex with two adjacent
neighbors, contrary to Lemma~\ref{lem:independent-neighborhood}(a).
In a further $4{,}368$, some choice of the four twins gives a bridge
with four or five attachments~\supp{E29}. In each exclusion the
recorded degree-three vertex or the four chosen twins lie outside
$\{a,b,c,d,e\}$, so adding vertices on the original triples preserves
their neighborhoods. In the second case, the component containing
the old component outside the same $\Psi_3$ still has all its
original attachments.

The $193$ remaining candidates give $965$ cases over the five choices
of $(n_c,n_e)$. Of these, $172$ are toroidal and $782$ have a proper
nontoroidal minor. The other $11$ give the five graphs in the
statement up to isomorphism~\supp{E29}.

R1.text:
\begin{lemma}\label{dis:faces}
Every torus embedding of $\Psi_1$ is cellular and has five faces.
For some $k\in\{1,2,3\}$, write
$\{i,j\}=\{1,2,3\}\setminus\{k\}$.
Omitting the twins from the boundary walks, these faces are
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\roman*)}]
\item two faces, each following
$s_iP_it_i,t_jP_j^{-1}s_j$ and meeting no other path.
\item one face following
$s_kP_kt_k,t_y,t_kP_k^{-1}s_k,s_x$, where
$x,y\in\{i,j\}$ may be equal.
\item two other faces meeting the paths exactly at
$\{s_k,s_{x'}\}$ and $\{t_k,t_{y'}\}$, respectively,
where $\{x,x'\}=\{y,y'\}=\{i,j\}$.
\end{enumerate}
All twelve choices of $k$, $x$ and $y$ occur.
\end{lemma}
\begin{proof}
The graph $\Psi_1$ is connected and nonplanar, as $\Psi_1-z$ is a subdivision of
$K_{3,3}$ with parts $A_1$ and $\{p,q,r\}$, so its torus embeddings are
cellular by Youngs's theorem. Subdividing an edge does not change the faces,
so we may take each $P_i$ to be an edge. Of the $1{,}024$ rotation
systems of this graph, $48$ have genus one. Up to automorphisms, these
give the two embeddings in Figure~\ref{fig:F-torus}~\supp{R1}. Their boundary walks,
after permuting the indices, give (i)--(iii), with $x=y$ in one and
$x\ne y$ in the other. Permuting the indices of both triples
simultaneously is an automorphism of $\Psi_1$, so the first gives the six
choices with $x=y$ and the second the six with $x\ne y$.

R2.text:
In (a), the unique bridge $B$ lies in a facial disk $F$ whose boundary
contains $a,b,c,d$. With the exception of $abcd$, every attachment
sequence of such a face of $\Psi_1/s_3t_3$ also occurs for $\Psi_1$,
up to cyclic shift and reversal~\supp{R2}. When the sequences agree,
a homeomorphism of the two disks matching the boundary appearances
carries the drawing of $B$ to the corresponding face of $\Psi_1$.

In (b), the bridge uses only $a,b,c$. Omitting $d$ from the
facial walks gives the same sequences containing $a,b,c$ for
$\Psi_1/s_3t_3$ and $\Psi_1$, up to cyclic shift and reversal~\supp{R2}.
Thus the bridge can be drawn in the corresponding face of $\Psi_1$.

The regions along $P_1$ in the two graphs are compared in~\supp{R2}.
If the region is an annulus, its boundary sequences are $ac\mid b$,
$ac\mid bd$, $a\mid b$ or $a\mid bd$. All four occur for $\Psi_1$, so
Lemma~\ref{lem:annulus-embedding} gives a torus embedding of $H$.

If the region is a disk, its sequence is $ab$, $abc$, $abd$, $abcd$
or $acdbdc$. The sequences $ab$ and $acdbdc$ also occur for $\Psi_1$.
In the disk with sequence $acdbdc$, the appearances after $b$ give
either $abc$ or $abd$ by using just $c$ or just $d$. Thus only $abcd$
with all four attachments remains.

R3.text:
Suppose neither $h_b$ nor $bc$ is present. Take a torus embedding
of $G/cf$ and identify the two boundary copies of $P_1$ in its
incident facial disks, keeping all other boundary appearances
distinct. The resulting region contains $P_1$ and every bridge
meeting its interior, hence all of $B$. Among the regions along
$P_1$ in $\Psi_1/cf$, those whose boundary contains $c,d$ are an
annulus with sequences $ac\mid bd$ and disks with sequence $acbdc$
or $acbcdc$. In each case no other face contains both $a,d$~\supp{R3},
so the region also contains $h_a$ or $ad$ if present.

R4.text:
Let $K$ consist of the added vertices, their incident edges and
the four attachments. Since the interior of $B$ is connected,
it must lie in one face of $K$ in any torus embedding of $G$.
We therefore need only consider faces whose boundary meets all
four attachments. For each rotation of $K$, \supp{R4} gives the
attachments in the order they occur on each boundary walk. We give
these sequences up to cyclic shift and reversal.
For the disk faces that occur, Lemma~\ref{cor:boundary-completions}
gives the planarity test by joining consecutive distinct
attachments on the boundary walk.

Let $B$ be an added bridge. Its interior is connected, so it lies in one disk face. Among the genus-one rotations with a walk containing $c,d$, no two labels alternate on a face meeting three or more attachments~\supp{R4}. Restrict the boundary sequence of the face containing $B$ to its three attachments. Combining consecutive equal appearances leaves $xyt$ or $xyxt$ up to relabeling. In both cases $x$ is consecutive with both $y$ and $t$, so Lemma~\ref{cor:boundary-completions} gives a plane drawing of $B+xy+xt$.

Retain $\Psi_2$, $B'$ and the star at $v$. Suppose this minor is toroidal. Since $B'$ joins $c,d$, Lemma~\ref{r2:cellular-center} rules out a genus-one regular neighborhood of $\Psi_2$. In genus zero the boundary sequences are $ab,ab,ac,bc,ad,bd$~\supp{R4}. Since $B'$ and the star each have three attachments, Lemma~\ref{lem:torus-complement} puts them in the same annulus. Together they meet all four vertices, so the boundary sequences are $ac\mid bd$ or $ad\mid bc$. By Lemma~\ref{lem:annulus-embedding}, adding $ac,bd$ or $ad,bc$, respectively, gives a plane drawing of $B'$ and the star. The star and the two added edges form a connected graph meeting $B'$ in its three attachments. Contract a spanning tree of this graph to those three vertices, keeping them distinct. This gives a planar two-edge completion of $B'$, a contradiction.

If $B'$ lies in a disk face, let $D$ be the disk representing that face. Otherwise a regular neighborhood of $\Psi_2$ has genus zero by Lemma~\ref{lem:torus-complement}. No boundary walk then contains three attachments or both $c,d$~\supp{R4}, so every bridge meets both boundary components of the unique annulus. Cut the annulus along $cd$ if present, or along a path through another bridge joining the two boundary components. This gives a disk $D$ without cutting the interior of $B'$.

By~\eqref{r1:availability}, $B_{ce}-a$ contains a $c$--$e$ path.
Contract it to a vertex $f$ and retain only $B_{bd}$ and the edges
at $p,q,r,z$. Fix a torus embedding of this proper minor. The edges
at the four twins form a copy $H$ of $\Psi_2$ with twin triples
$\{a,b,f\}$ and $\{a,d,f\}$. Since $B$ joins $b,d$ and has no
planar completion by two edges, Lemma~\ref{r2:cellular-center}
forces a closed regular neighborhood of $H$ to have genus zero.
Its boundary sequences are $ab,bf,ad,df,af,af$~\supp{R4}.
Every bridge in $B_{bd}$ and the edge $bd$ if present meet both
$b,d$. As no boundary walk contains both, all lie in the unique
annulus given by Lemma~\ref{lem:torus-complement}. Its two boundary
walks contain $b$ and $d$, respectively, so the two $af$ walks
bound disks.

R5.text:
\begin{lemma}\label{r2:degree-four}
No three-connected obstruction has twin pairs with neighborhoods $\{a,b,c\},\{a,b,d\}$ and $\deg(b)=4$.
\end{lemma}
\begin{proof}
Suppose $\deg(b)=4$. Every component outside $\Psi_2$
then has neighborhood $\{a,c,d\}$ by three-connectivity.
Let $B_1$ consist of their bridges and $cd$, if present,
so $G=\Psi_2\cup B_1$. By minimality, $G-z$ has a torus
embedding. All bridges in $B_1$ lie in the same face $F$
of $H=\Psi_2-z$, since each meets $d$ and $\deg_H(d)=1$. Record only $a,c,d$ on the boundary walks of $F$.
If consecutive appearances are equal, move their incident
edges to one appearance along the intervening boundary arc,
preserving their order. Since $B_1$ meets both $c,d$,
the rotation table~\supp{R5} and
Lemma~\ref{lem:torus-complement} leave only the disk sequences
$acd,acad,acacd$ and the annular pairs $ad\mid ac,ad\mid c$. We show that $B_1$ can be drawn in an annulus with $a_1,d$
on one boundary and $a_2,c$ on the other, allowing the edges
at $a$ to use $a_1$ or $a_2$. The annular cases already give
this, with $a_2$ unused for $ad\mid c$. In a disk case,
separate the appearances and use the boundary order
$a_1,c_1,a_2,c_2,d$, leaving positions unused where needed.
Draw $c_1c_2,c_1a_2,a_1d$ outside the disk without crossings,
then contract $c_1c_2$ to recover $c$. The resulting graph
is planar, with $a_1,a_2$ distinct and $a_1d,a_2c$ added.
Lemma~\ref{lem:annulus-embedding} gives the required drawing (Figure~\ref{fig:psi2-annulus-construction}(d)--(f)). A planar embedding of $\Psi_2$ has faces $apcqa$ and $ardza$.
Remove an open disk from each and join the new boundary
circles by a cylinder. This gives a torus embedding with
an annular face $ac\mid ad$. Insert the drawing of $B_1$,
with the edges at $a_2$ reaching $a$ between $ap,aq$ and
those at $a_1$ reaching $a$ between $ar,az$.
This embeds $G$ on the torus (Figure~\ref{fig:psi2-annulus-construction}(a)--(c)), a contradiction.

R6.text:
\begin{lemma}\label{r1:exterior-faces}
In a torus embedding of $\Psi_3$, let $\mathcal N$ be a closed regular
neighborhood of $\Psi_3$. If $\mathcal N$ has genus one and a face meets
$b,c,d,e$, that face is a disk with attachment sequence
$a,b,a,d,a,c,a,e$, up to cyclic shift and reversal, and the other
two faces have attachment sequences $bc,de$. If $\mathcal N$ has genus zero, any face
meeting $b,c,d,e$ is an annulus with attachment sequences $bc\mid de$, and
the other three faces are disks with attachment sequences $axay$, $ax'$ and
$ay'$, where $\{x,x'\}=\{b,c\}$ and $\{y,y'\}=\{d,e\}$.
\end{lemma}
\begin{proof}
For each of the $96$ rotation systems of $\Psi_3$, the table in~\supp{R6} gives the attachments in order along each facial walk. No rotation system of genus zero has a face containing all four of $b,c,d,e$ in its boundary walk. The only pair of facial walks in any rotation system of genus zero whose union contains all four has attachment sequences $bc,de$. Thus, by Lemma~\ref{lem:torus-complement}, a face meeting all four in a torus embedding with this rotation must be an annulus with attachment sequences $bc\mid de$. The other three facial walks of such a rotation have attachment sequences $axay$, $ax'$ and $ay'$, and bound disks by the same lemma. Of the genus-one rotations, the only facial attachment sequence containing all four is $abadacae$, up to cyclic shift and reversal. The other two faces have attachment sequences $bc,de$.

R7.text:
Suppose $B_1+ab+ad$ is planar.
Lemma~\ref{core:three-root-cut} gives twins $p',q'$
whose neighborhood $X$ contains $a$. Since $X$ meets
each of $\{a,b,c\},\{a,d,e\}$ exactly once, it has
the form $\{a,u,v\}$ with
$u,v\in\operatorname{Int}(B_1)$. The same lemma gives
disjoint $b$--$u$ and $d$--$v$ paths.
Choose $p',q',r,z$ as the four twins.
The set $\operatorname{Int}(B)\cup\{b,c,p,q\}$ is
connected because $c$ has a neighbor in the interior of $B$
and $p,q$ join $b$ to $c$. It lies in a component
outside the new $\Psi_3$, with neighbors at $a,d,e$
through $B$ and at $u$ through the $b$--$u$ path.
Since five attachments are excluded, its bridge
has exactly four attachments and at least
$|\operatorname{Int}(B)|+4$ interior vertices, contrary to
the choice of $B$. Thus $B_1+ab+ad$ is nonplanar, and it has no $K_5$ minor.
Let $B_1'$ be an allowed minor of $B_1$ with $B_1'+ab+ad$
nonplanar. Contract the interior of $B$ to $w$
and keep only $\Psi_3$, $B_1'$ and the edges at $w$.
The resulting minor is $\Psi_3\cup B_1'+w$, where
$N(w)=\{a,c,d,e\}$. The graph $\Psi_3+w$ contains $K_{3,3}$ with
parts $\{a,d,e\}$ and $\{r,z,w\}$. Thus, in every torus
embedding of $\Psi_3+w$, each component of the complement
of its closed regular neighborhood is a disk by
Lemma~\ref{lem:torus-complement}.
In every such embedding, a facial walk containing
$a,b,d$ has attachment sequence $abad$, up to
cyclic shift and reversal~\supp{R7}.
Lemma~\ref{cor:boundary-completions} therefore
requires $B_1'+ab+ad$ to be planar, a contradiction.
Hence this minor is nontoroidal. Taking $B_1'=B_1$, minimality
gives $G=\Psi_3\cup B_1+w$, and
Corollary~\ref{common:reduced-forms}, with attachments
$a,b,d$ and added edges $ab,ad$, gives
$349$ possibilities for $B_1$. These are the $349$ forms of
Proposition~\ref{r1:missing-a-outcome} again. Every resulting graph
has a $K_5$ minor, a cut of at most two vertices,
or a proper nontoroidal minor~\supp{E23}.
Thus every other bridge with nonempty interior
has planar triangle completion, and
Lemma~\ref{lem:flat-replacement} makes its interior
a single vertex.
\end{proof}

R8.text:
Indeed, the rotation tables in~\supp{R8} give the boundary sequences for all twelve choices of $G-\operatorname{Int}(B)$. For each disk face meeting all four attachments, Lemma~\ref{cor:boundary-completions} gives the test by joining consecutive distinct attachments in its boundary sequence. Only the first row with $n_e=2$ admits a genus-zero rotation. No single boundary walk then meets all four attachments. The only
pair of boundary sequences that together contain all four is
$ac\mid de$, giving the test $B+ac+de$ by
Lemma~\ref{lem:annulus-embedding}. Keeping the inclusion-minimal edge sets gives the table.

R9.text:
By~\eqref{r1:availability}, $ce$ is an edge or is supplied by a
component outside $\Psi_3$. Since $e$ is not an attachment of $B$,
shortening the corresponding $c$--$e$ path to $ce$ gives
$(\Psi_3\cup B)+ce$ as a minor of $G$. Consider a torus embedding
of this minor. In a genus-one rotation of $\Psi_3+ce$, the
sequences on $b,c,d$ along facial walks meeting all three are
$bcd$ and $bcdc$. For a planar rotation,
no boundary walk contains all three attachments, and the only possible
annuli are $bc\mid ad$ and $bc\mid de$~\supp{R9}. In each disk sequence
$b,c$ are consecutive, and in each annulus they form one boundary
sequence. Thus Lemmas~\ref{cor:boundary-completions}
and~\ref{lem:annulus-embedding} require $B+bc$ to be planar in every
case. The minor is therefore nontoroidal, so by minimality it is $G$.

R10.text: It remains to consider $B_1$ on $\{a,b,d\}$. Contract the interior of $B$ to $w$, delete $aw$, and retain only $\Psi_3$, $B_1$ and the edges $cw,dw,ew$. This proper minor is toroidal. Let $K$ consist of $\Psi_3$ and the three edges at $w$. It contains a $K_{3,3}$ subdivision with parts $\{a,d,e\}$ and $\{r,z,w\}$, using $apcw$ for the $a$--$w$ branch. Thus every face of $K$ in the torus embedding is a disk by Lemma~\ref{lem:torus-complement}. On any face containing $a,b,d$, the boundary sequence restricted to these three vertices is $abad$~\supp{R10}. Since $B_1$ lies in such a face, Lemma~\ref{cor:boundary-completions} gives a plane drawing of $B_1+ab+ad$.

In each of these four minors the graph outside $\operatorname{Int}(B)$
is nonplanar, so every face in a torus embedding of that graph is a
disk. On a facial walk meeting $a,b,d$, the sequence restricted to
these vertices is $abad$, with $abd$ also possible when
$N(v)=\{a,c,d\}$~\supp{R10}. Both require $B+ab+ad$ to
be planar by Lemma~\ref{cor:boundary-completions}. Thus the retained
minor is nontoroidal and by minimality is $G$. The same test applies
to every allowed minor of $B$, so Corollary~\ref{common:reduced-forms}
gives $349$ forms with added edges $ab,ad$ for each of the four
choices of $N(v)$. All but two of the resulting graphs have a proper
nontoroidal minor. Both exceptions have $N(v)=\{c,d,e\}$ and
$B+ad+bd$ planar~\supp{E27}, contrary to hypothesis.

R11.text:
It remains to rule out a bridge on $\{b,c,d\}$ and the edge $cd$.
In either case we may retain $(\Psi_3\cup B)+ce$ as above. In the
first case also retain the bridge with its interior contracted to a
vertex adjacent to $b,c,d$. In the second retain $cd$. Call the
resulting minor $H_1$. In both cases $H_1-\operatorname{Int}(B)$
is nonplanar. In its torus embeddings, the sequences on $a,b,d$
along facial walks meeting all three are $abad,adbd,abd$~\supp{R11}. The first
two give the completions $B+ab+ad$ and $B+ad+bd$, respectively.
The triangle completion for $abd$ contains both. Thus
Lemma~\ref{cor:boundary-completions} gives
\begin{equation}\label{r1:two-cap-test}
H_1\text{ is toroidal}\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
B+ab+ad\text{ is planar or }B+ad+bd\text{ is planar}.
\end{equation}
Both completions are nonplanar, so $G=H_1$ by minimality. The same
test holds after replacing $B$ by any allowed minor. Hence no proper
allowed minor keeps both completions nonplanar.
